codebook.name: financial stress
codebook.definition: Expressions of anxiety, worry, or cognitive burden directly related to money.
codebook.inclusion_criteria: Must reference money, cost, financial resources, or economic state.
codebook.exclusion_criteria: General academic stress not linked to finances.
codebook.example_anchor: I count every penny. I can't focus because I'm thinking about the electricity bill.

codebook.name: guilt and obligation
codebook.definition: Sense of debt, responsibility, or guilt tied to family sacrifice.
codebook.inclusion_criteria: References to parental sacrifice, duty, letting family down.
codebook.exclusion_criteria: General academic pressure without familial framing.
codebook.example_anchor: If I fail it's not just my failure, it's hers too.

codebook.name: class invisibility
codebook.definition: Experiences of social exclusion, othering, or class-based otherness.
codebook.inclusion_criteria: Comparisons with peers, feeling different, hiding socioeconomic status.
codebook.example_anchor: There's this invisible wall between me and them.

codebook.name: material constraint
codebook.definition: Concrete resource deprivations affecting study (textbooks, food, time).
codebook.inclusion_criteria: Specific material lacks: food, books, transport, equipment, time from work.
codebook.example_anchor: I can't afford the textbooks. I skip lunch some days.

codebook.name: support system failure
codebook.definition: Institutional failures to make support visible, accessible, or dignified.
codebook.inclusion_criteria: Unawareness of support, humiliating processes, inaccessible information.
codebook.example_anchor: I didn't know about the hardship fund for two years.

codebook.name: identity code-switching
codebook.definition: Effortful performance of a different class identity to fit in.
codebook.inclusion_criteria: References to masking, pretending, hiding, being silent.
codebook.example_anchor: You're constantly code-switching, hiding how hard things actually are.

codebook.name: aspirational persistence
codebook.definition: Motivation and resilience despite hardship, linked to pride and goals.
codebook.inclusion_criteria: Language of continuing, pride, being here, not giving up.

themes.name: The Weight of Gratitude
themes.central_concept: Gratitude-debt as a driver of aspirational persistence under financial hardship
themes.narrative: Participants do not experience financial hardship as a purely economic phenomenon. It is deeply entangled with emotional obligations to families who have sacrificed materially for their university attendance. This creates a paradoxical affective state: pride in aspiration co-exists with paralysing guilt. Participants persist despite hardship not in spite of this guilt but, in part, because of it — the debt of gratitude functioning as a form of resilience fuel.
quotes: "I keep going even when I'm exhausted. But sometimes I can't focus in lectures because I'm thinking about the electricity bill." — P1
negative_cases: P3 expresses pride without guilt framing — suggests obligation is not universal; may be moderated by degree of visible parental sacrifice.

themes.name: Material Poverty, Epistemic Exclusion
themes.central_concept: Structural inaccessibility of support as a second-order form of poverty
themes.narrative: First-generation students face a double disadvantage: they lack material resources (food, textbooks, time) and they lack the cultural capital to navigate institutional support systems. Support mechanisms exist but are invisible by design — buried in websites, requiring students to already know the language of the university. This constitutes a form of structural exclusion that compounds material deprivation.
quotes: "I can't afford the textbooks. I use the library but sometimes they're all checked out. My classmates just buy them on their laptops." — P1
"I didn't know about the hardship fund for two years. Nobody told me." — P2
negative_cases: P1 does access the library — not entirely excluded; resourcefulness and workarounds exist.

themes.name: The Invisible Tax of Class
themes.central_concept: Code-switching as an invisible cognitive tax on first-generation students
themes.narrative: Participants describe a continuous, effortful performance of class identity in order to pass as 'normal' students. This code-switching — staying silent about the warehouse job, the electricity bill, the skipped meal — is cognitively and emotionally costly. The invisibility is not merely social but also cognitive: energy spent hiding is energy not spent learning.
quotes: "You're constantly code-switching, hiding how hard things actually are. The invisibility is exhausting." — P3
"There's this invisible wall between me and them." — P1
negative_cases: P2 does not use code-switching language; may resist or not conceptualise experience this way — or may have greater economic confidence despite hardship.
